fixes.title: Connection troubleshooter said it 'couldn't pin down the exact cause' while holding an error that named the exact cause, then gave four irrelevant hardware steps
fixes.summary: Confirmed the verifier's location correction: the dialog only renders; the classifier and knowledge base are packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/models/troubleshooter/connection_diagnostic.dart. The built-in guider's preflight messages (all six start 'Built-in guider requires ...', native/skotiq_native/bridge/src/builtin_guider.rs:1265-1330) matched no marker table, so _classify fell through to DiagnosticCategory.unknown -> headline "The connection didn't complete", body 'we couldn't pin down the exact cause', and _unknownSteps' four hardware steps: reseat the cable, confirm power, close other programs, restart Skotiq. The built-in guider is SOFTWARE - it reuses the imaging camera and pulses the mount - so it has no cable and no power switch; those steps cannot work and the operator concludes the app is broken. Added a first-party preflight marker list checked BEFORE every driver-shaped marker (our own setup checks are never a cable, a COM registration or a firewall), routing to DiagnosticCategory.configuration; threaded the normalized error into _headlineFor/_plainLanguageFor/_stepsFor so the configuration branch can name the actual value. New copy: headline 'Your equipment profile is missing a value', body explaining the guider is software with no cable to check, and steps keyed on which value the check named - focal length -> 'Open Equipment -> your active profile -> Edit' + 'Enter the Focal Length of the scope you are guiding with' (mm) + 'Save the profile, then connect the guider again'; pixel size -> the imaging camera reported 0; binning -> guide binning; connected camera/mount -> assign and connect both in the active profile.
fixes.test: Two levels. RENDERED: packages/skotiq_app/test/widgets/troubleshooter/connection_troubleshooter_dialog_test.dart - 'the built-in guider preflight renders the setting, not a cable' opens the real dialog with the verbatim focal_length_mm=0 message and asserts the screen shows no "couldn't pin down", no 'Reseat the cable', no 'Restart Skotiq', and does show 'Focal Length' (7/7 pass). MODEL: packages/skotiq_core/test/models/connection_diagnostic_test.dart - new group 'built-in guider preflight', 5 tests: the focal_length_mm=0 message classifies as configuration and the body no longer contains "couldn't pin down"; the STEPS contain 'focal length' and contain neither 'cable' nor 'power' nor 'restart skotiq' (asserted against a new _stepsText helper, because the explanation deliberately says there is no cable); the sibling 'requires an active profile with a guide focal length' variant classifies the same; the 'requires a connected camera in the active profile' variant names the profile and no cable; and the anti-inversion case - a real ASCOM guider 0x800706ba still gets the driver playbook, so the new rule cannot swallow genuine hardware failures on the same device type. 44/44 pass.

fixes.title: Closing the First Light dialog mid-capture orphaned the exposure, and there was no cancel inside the dialog
fixes.summary: Four parts, because the defect had four. (1) There was NO cancel path at all: FirstLightOrchestrator.run and firstLightControllerProvider had only reset(), which clears the UI state while the sensor keeps exposing. Added FirstLightOrchestrator.cancel() -> imagingServiceProvider.cancelExposure() (the same seam the exposure was started through; it resolves the pending exposure completer AND dispatches the driver abort) plus a per-run _cancelRequested latch checked after each stage, so a cancel during stretch/solve/annotate stops there too. A cancel unwinds via a dedicated _FirstLightCancelled to IDLE, not to `failed` — an operator-requested stop is not a pipeline failure, and the capture path would otherwise have reported 'Capture failed: the camera returned no image'. The latch is cleared at the top of run() so it cannot leak into the next run. (2) FirstLightController.cancel() delegates, guarded on the in-flight flag. (3) The dialog's running phases now render a 'Stop capture' footer action wired to that cancel; previously _actionsFor returned null for all four. (4) The header ✕ was the one hole PopScope did not cover — SkotiqDialog calls Navigator.pop directly — so the dialog now passes closeEnabled: !state.isRunning. Separately, the verifier proved the Imaging viewer's 'Abort capture' X was genuinely dead for this path: imaging_preview_toolbar decides to SHOW it from the GLOBAL exposureProgressProvider, while _abortCapture early-returned on `if (!_isSingleCapture && !_isLooping) return;` — screen-local flags a first-light (or centering, or sequencer) exposure never sets. The abort now always targets the shared imaging service; the local _isStoppingCapture latch is set only when this screen owns the capture, because that flag is cleared in the capture methods' finally, which never runs for a foreign exposure and would have hidden the button for the rest of the session (relocating the defect).
fixes.test: Three files. (a) skotiq_core/test/services/first_light_cancel_test.dart — 3 tests against a stalled imaging service: cancel raises cancelExposure exactly once AND the flow ends at FirstLightPhase.idle with no errorMessage; a cancel with no run in flight aborts nothing; and a cancel does not leak into the next run (the second run must still reach `failed`, which a stale latch would swallow). (b) skotiq_app/test/widgets/first_light/first_light_flow_dialog_test.dart — 3 tests: the running phase's SkotiqDialog has closeEnabled false, its ✕ IconButton has onPressed null, and TAPPING it leaves FirstLightFlowDialog mounted; the running phase's 'Stop capture' button calls controller.cancel(); and a terminal phase is still closable with no Stop button (anti-inversion — the gate must not strand the operator in a finished dialog). (c) skotiq_app/test/screens/imaging/imaging_abort_foreign_exposure_test.dart — pumps the real ImagingScreen, arms exposureProgressProvider WITHOUT the screen starting a capture, asserts the abort button is offered, that tapping it reaches cancelExposure, that the button is still offered afterwards (no permanent latch), and that it disappears when the progress really ends. 16/16 first_light + 2/2 imaging-abort pass.
fixes.caveats: Two honest limits. (1) The cancel is immediate for the EXPOSURE stage (cancelExposure resolves the pending completer and dispatches the driver abort). During stretch/solve/annotate the latch only takes effect at the next checkpoint, so a hung plate solve keeps the dialog up until it returns or times out. That is not a new stuck-ness: PopScope(canPop: !state.isRunning) already blocked Escape and the barrier during those stages before this change, and there is now an exit where there was none. (2) The imaging-toolbar abort now genuinely stops a sequencer or centering exposure too, not just a first-light one. That is a real behavioural expansion — the button previously did nothing for those — and it is what the button's own label and tooltip promise, but it was verified in a widget test with a fake service, not against a live sequencer run.
fixes.revert_check: Three separate reverts, each at the production call site. (1) Deleted `_ref.read(imagingServiceProvider).cancelExposure();` from FirstLightOrchestrator.cancel — flutter test test/services/first_light_cancel_test.dart -> +1 -2 ('cancel aborts the exposure at the camera and unwinds to idle' and 'a cancel does not leak into the next run' both failed). (2) Deleted `closeEnabled: !state.isRunning,` from the dialog -> 'running phase disables the header close button' failed (+14 -1). (3) Replaced the running-phase `return [SkotiqButton(label: 'Stop capture' ...)]` with `return null` -> 'running phase offers a stop that cancels at the camera' failed (+14 -1). (4) Re-inserted `if (!_isSingleCapture && !_isLooping) return;` at the top of _abortCapture -> 'the abort reaches the camera for an exposure this screen did not start' failed. All restored; 16/16 + 2/2 green.
